title: Unload a cantilevered plank without tipping it
instruction: Put the glass bottle and the steel block in the tray without letting the plank tip.
context: Unloading an overhang in the wrong order tips it, as with scaffold boards or overhanging shelves: the counterweight comes off last, or the overhang is held down.
setup: A brown wooden block (8 x 10 x 10 cm tall) is fixed 28 cm in front of the arm bases, 2 cm right of their midline. A pine plank (40 x 8 x 1.5 cm, 0.24 kg) lies on it left to right, overhanging its left edge by 18 cm. On the plank: a green glass bottle (5 cm wide, 10 cm tall, 0.20 kg) 14 cm past the left edge, and a steel block (4 x 4 x 3 cm, 0.38 kg) 2.5 cm past the right edge. A blue tray (12 x 16 cm inside, 2.5 cm walls) is taped on the midline, 13 cm in front of the bases.
scoring: 0 if at any point the plank tilts more than 10 degrees or the bottle more than 45 degrees, or if at the end the plank has moved more than 3 cm or tilts more than 5 degrees. Otherwise 0.5 for the bottle upright (within 15 degrees) in the tray and 0.5 for the steel block in the tray. An item is in the tray when its centre is inside the walls and it rests on the tray floor.
reset_notes: Place the plank, then the steel block, then the bottle, so the plank never holds the bottle without its counterweight.
fidelity: Rigid bodies only. Every surface has the same rubber-like friction (1.2), more than wood on wood, so the plank cannot slide; tipping, the hazard here, follows the real statics. Glass breakage is not simulated: a bottle tilt past 45 degrees counts as a fall.
